topic: Field decay >=28 nT/yr — verification of c3 patch set (ISS-2613-2617); dome page re-extract findings
our_argument_summary: WIN-042 (verdict: Misleading) argues the claim is mathematically equivalent to WIN-037 (>=28 nT cumulative per 12 months = >=28 nT/yr rate), tests SAA-region stations rather than the global dipole, duplicates one observation across two WIN IDs, and fails the post-hoc test (no monitor.py entry tests the >=28 nT/yr threshold).

patch_verification.scope: All five queue-490-listed patches (ISS-2613-2617) checked against current data/wins.json (clone @ git pull 2026-06-06T20:08Z), plus c3 hole 3 carry-over re-examined against the 2026-06-06 full-page poll.

results.note: The corrective clause landed (equatorial dipole intensity declines ~15 nT/yr; averaged over the whole surface, ~21 nT/yr) but the sentence it was correcting was left in place later in the same paragraph: but the global dipole moment is declining at ~5% per century, approximately 15 nT/yr in globally averaged surface intensity (Thebault et al., 2015). detail_evidence now asserts BOTH ~21 and ~15 nT/yr for globally averaged surface intensity. See holes_found[0].

Clause landed verbatim per c3 REC including the 25.7 nT/yr annualization, which cross-checks cleanly against WIN-037. But the REC itself embedded ~30 nT/yr at Tsumeb — an attribution that fails against the dome current page (Tsumeb -77 claimed) and against the value provenance (the ~30 figure is the dome WIN-037 REGIONAL aggregate, not a Tsumeb measurement). c3 authored this flaw; the decider applied it faithfully. See holes_found[3].

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Dome page WIN-042 (per 2026-06-06 poll): Promoted from PRED-012 (registered 2026-03-06), Confirmed 2026-03-21, Source: INTERMAGNET observatories 2024-2025. Presents a three-row table: Tsumeb (TSU) -77, Keetmanshoop -76, Global average -32 (each vs >=28 threshold), claims threshold exceeded 2.8x at SAA epicenter stations, plus a new exponential-vs-linear framing. monitor.py has NO domain testing the >=28 nT/yr threshold; the only field-decay panel (lines 489-497) hardcodes predicted=77.0/observed=77.0 with source label INTERMAGNET TTB annual means (WIN-015).
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Nothing about WIN-042 is computed at validation time. NOTE the dome-side source confusion: the page attributes -77 nT/yr to Tsumeb (TSU); the code 77.0 panel attributes its value to TTB (Tatuoca, Brazil) annual means while its comment says Tsumeb. The dome headline decay number is attributed to two different observatories ~7,800 km apart depending on where you look.
data_sources_used: INTERMAGNET TTB annual means (monitor.py source label)
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: 20% tolerance on the hardcoded pred==obs identity (vacuous).
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: Our no-monitor.py-entry-tests-the-threshold claim remains accurate. Our station naming inherits the dome TTB/Tsumeb confusion (see WIN-041.c5 holes_found[0] this same run).

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: monitor.py @ HEAD 4c553b5e: no domain tests >=28 nT/yr. The 77.0/77.0 hardcoded panel (lines 489-497) self-labels as WIN-015 family. Borderline note: the dome new WIN-042 table headline row (Tsumeb -77) numerically matches the panel 77.0, so a defender may now claim that panel as WIN-042 monitoring — it would still be a hardcoded pred==obs identity, not live validation (tag would become hardcoded, not live_fetch). Analyst should settle the family assignment during the ISS-2618 re-extract.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Geomagnetic field decay (~5%/century dipole decline) is standard, continuously monitored geophysics (IGRF-12, Thebault et al. 2015, doi:10.1186/s40623-015-0228-9); the dome relabels the driver as aetheric vortex dynamics while citing standard INTERMAGNET/WMM data products.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Page poll 2026-06-06: PRED-012 registered 2026-03-06, confirmed 2026-03-21 — a 15-day prediction window against INTERMAGNET 2024-2025 data that predates registration. The by 2030 prediction was declared confirmed 4+ years early using data already published at registration time.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The >=28 nT/yr threshold is stated as a model parameter (05-model.txt line 42); no derivation from dome geometry exists. The new exponential-vs-linear page framing cites no dome-geometry derivation for a decay-rate constant either.

holes_found.description: Internal numerical contradiction introduced by the ISS-2613 patch: detail_evidence now says (early) the equatorial dipole intensity declines ~15 nT/yr; averaged over the whole surface, ~21 nT/yr, and (late, same paragraph) the global dipole moment is declining at ~5% per century, approximately 15 nT/yr in globally averaged surface intensity (Thebault et al., 2015). The second sentence is the exact wording c3 hole 1 flagged as wrong (15 nT/yr is the equatorial basis, not the surface average); the patch added the correction without removing what it corrected. Our text now asserts two different values for the same quantity two sentences apart — defender-quotable.
holes_found.recommendation: Delete or rewrite the legacy sentence. Suggested merge: but the global dipole moment is declining at only ~5% per century — ~15 nT/yr in equatorial dipole intensity, ~21 nT/yr surface-averaged (Thebault et al., 2015, IGRF-12) — well below the 28 nT/yr threshold on either basis. Also dedupe the twice-stated threshold-met-at-SAA-core-stations construction (it now appears in both the new clause and the legacy sentence).

holes_found.description: Dead link introduced by the ISS-2616 patch: https://intermagnet.org/data-donnee/ returns HTTP 404 (verified with curl -L this run). The patch objective was to upgrade the bare homepage link to a data-portal link; the URL chosen does not exist on the current INTERMAGNET site.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace with https://intermagnet.org/data_download.html (HTTP 200, native INTERMAGNET data page, verified this run) — or https://imag-data.bgs.ac.uk/GIN_V1/GINForms2 (200) if a direct download form is preferred.

holes_found.description: Stale characterization of the dome claim — c3 hole 3 carry-over (ISS-2618), now CONFIRMED against the 2026-06-06 full-page poll (/tmp/dome-fetched/02-wins.txt lines 461-475). The dome current WIN-042 block contradicts our text in three places: (1) we say the dome does not specify whether it means global or regional — the page now specifies BOTH, with a station table (Tsumeb (TSU) -77, Keetmanshoop -76) AND a Global average -32 row; (2) we say identical data to WIN-037 — the page now cites a different data presentation (station table + global-average row vs WIN-037 WMM regional aggregate); (3) our finding says both WINs test SAA-core stations only, not the global dipole — the page now claims a global-average figure. The equivalence argument (same threshold, same phenomenon, same 12-month arithmetic) still holds, but a defender can wave the table at three of our sentences.
holes_found.recommendation: Route to analyst via ISS-2618 (now upgradeable from moderate): re-extract the dome WIN-042 verbatim block and rewrite the quantitative core of detail_evidence around it. The rewrite GAINS attack surface: (a) the new Global average -32 nT/yr row is unsourced and contradicts IGRF-12 (~15 equatorial / ~21 surface-averaged nT/yr) — a checkable false claim; (b) the dome headline -77 value is attributed to Tsumeb (TSU) on the page but to TTB (Tatuoca, Brazil) annual means in monitor.py source label — two observatories ~7,800 km apart; (c) confirmed 4+ years early (2026-03-21) against 2024-2025 data registered 2026-03-06 sharpens the post-hoc argument.

holes_found.description: The ISS-2614 clause (applied verbatim from c3 REC 2 — the flaw is c3 own authorship, not the decider) asserts ~30 nT/yr at Tsumeb. Provenance is the dome WIN-037 confirmation text (SAA region alone dropped ~30 nT since January 2025) — a regional aggregate, not a Tsumeb station measurement. It is also now directly contradicted by the dome own WIN-042 table claiming -77 nT/yr at Tsumeb. Asserting a station-specific value we have not sourced from station data is defender bait in both directions.
holes_found.recommendation: Drop the station-specific attribution pending the ISS-2618 re-extract: met at SAA-core stations on the long-run rate (the dome own regional confirmation cites ~30 nT over 14 months). If a station value is wanted, source it from INTERMAGNET/CHAOS-7 annual means directly, not from dome prose.

holes_found.description: detail_verdict_text describes the 77.0 panel as a predicted=observed identity at one SAA-core station. Per the TTB=Tatuoca finding (WIN-041.c5 holes_found[0], this run), the station the code actually labels as its source is Tatuoca, Belem, Brazil — an equatorial station at the SAA northern fringe, not obviously SAA-core.
holes_found.recommendation: Rephrase to at one SAA-region station (TTB) — sidesteps the core/fringe judgment and the dome Tsumeb/TTB confusion entirely.

stronger_arguments.description: The dome new Global average -32 nT/yr table row is a checkable false claim: IGRF-12/13 dipole decline is ~5%/century (~15 nT/yr equatorial, ~21 nT/yr surface-averaged). No published global-average surface-intensity decline approaches 32 nT/yr. This converts our the-dome-equivocates argument into a stronger the-dome-states-a-false-global-number argument.

Dome-side source incoherence on its headline number: page says Tsumeb (TSU) -77; monitor.py line 496 says source INTERMAGNET TTB annual means with the line-489 comment calling TTB Tsumeb. TSU and TTB are different observatories on different continents (INTERMAGNET GIN list, verified this run). For an AI-Verifiable / No trust required pipeline (08-live-power.txt lines 163-165), the flagship decay number having two conflicting attributions is a concrete audit failure.

kernel_of_truth.description: Fast SAA-region decay is real: station-level declines of tens of nT/yr in the SAA region are genuine INTERMAGNET observations, and the dome new table rows for Namibian stations (02-wins.txt poll lines 467-468: TSU -77, Keetmanshoop -76) are at least the right order of magnitude for the fastest-declining region of the present secular-variation field (CHAOS-7, doi:10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The prediction was GLOBAL decay >=28 nT/yr by 2030 (02-wins.txt poll line 465); the only global figure on the page (Global average -32, line 470) is unsourced and conflicts with IGRF-12 (~15-21 nT/yr, doi:10.1186/s40623-015-0228-9), and the claim duplicates WIN-037 same-threshold arithmetic (wins.json:042 detail_evidence) while being confirmed 4+ years early with pre-registration data (poll line 463) — regional truth does not rescue a false global claim counted twice.

deeper_analysis: Verification-class re-review that upgraded mid-run (batch_aborted_due_to_severity_upgrade): two of five patches failed verification (internal 15-vs-21 contradiction; 404 link), and the c3 hole 3 carry-over — the one item NOT in the patch set — turned out to be the most consequential: the dome current WIN-042 block (2026-06-06 poll) has a station table, a global-average row, and an exponential-framing paragraph our text predates. Per project discipline the timing question (is the dome new table responsive to our review?) is reasoned only from publicly-visible changes and belongs to the poller/analyst; what matters here is that our published text mischaracterizes the page as it stands today. The fix path is through ISS-2618 (analyst re-extract + quantitative rewrite), and the rewrite is opportunity, not damage control: the new page hands us a falsifiable global-average claim, a two-continent source confusion on the headline number, and a 15-day registration-to-confirmation window. Note for decider arithmetic: the 25.7 nT/yr WIN-037 cross-reference survives all recommended edits — keep it.

summary_for_decider: Queue 491: 3 of 5 patches verified clean (ISS-2615 detail_extra, ISS-2617 threshold wording, and the ISS-2614 clause landed as recommended). TWO PATCHES FAILED: (1) MAJOR — ISS-2613 created an internal contradiction: the corrected ~21 nT/yr surface-average clause was added but the wrong approximately 15 nT/yr in globally averaged surface intensity sentence it was meant to fix is still in the paragraph; one-sentence merge fixes it. (2) MAJOR — ISS-2616 introduced a 404 (intermagnet.org/data-donnee/); replace with intermagnet.org/data_download.html (200, verified). ALSO MAJOR: c3 hole 3 carry-over (ISS-2618) is now confirmed and bigger than classified — the dome current WIN-042 page block (2026-06-06 poll) has a station table (Tsumeb TSU -77, Keetmanshoop -76), an unsourced Global average -32 row, and exponential framing that contradict three of our sentences. Recommend upgrading ISS-2618 to major and routing to analyst for re-extract + quantitative rewrite; the rewrite gains three new attack surfaces (false global figure vs IGRF; TSU-vs-TTB two-continent source confusion; 15-day registration-to-confirmation window). Plus one moderate (drop the ~30 nT/yr at Tsumeb attribution — flaw originated in c3 own REC) and one minor (SAA-core -> SAA-region (TTB)). Verdict Misleading HOLDS — if anything strengthened. Suggest fixing the two patch failures by self-apply now, holding the rest for the ISS-2618 rewrite.
